provenance: T-M40-2-6, P1, open since PR #46 R6. `parse_plan` validated that the top level is a list and nothing below it, so `[None]` and `["extract WebArea"]` were plans as far as the executor was concerned; `plan_gap` no longer raises on those (both clauses guarded, `plan-gap-truth-table` rows), and the step loop then read `step["action"]` off a string. The TypeError propagated out of `run_task` — no status, no failure class, none of the taxonomy — and only `server.py:_execute`'s catch-all turned it into `failure:env` for a deployed run, while an eval-adapter caller got the raw exception. Not a regression: `main` at d06a569 reaches the same line the same way. The fix is in TWO places and neither is redundant: `parse_plan` covers the live planner (graded by `planner-fenced-json`'s `also_rejects`), and the executor covers every offline case, because `stub_planner` is injected at exactly the boundary `parse_plan` guards — a malformed plan reaches the step loop without ever passing through it. This case is the repro the block names, verbatim, and it takes the executor path. `expect.actions: 1` pins that the run spent the pre-plan navigation and nothing else: a plan the executor cannot honour is refused before it acts, which is what `failure:task` means in specs/000.

triage.red_first: RED before the guard, and not as a failed assertion — the adapter propagated `TypeError: string indices must be integers, not 'str'` out of `run_case`, which is the defect itself: the harness had no verdict to compare because the run never produced one.
triage.note: Tagged `invariant` because it is inv1's own property (one failure class, always) rather than a claim about any one run — an uncaught exception is the one shape that has NO class. `hello.html` on purpose: the smallest fixture in the tree, so nothing about the page can be the reason this passes or fails.
